I've had some less than desirable phone experiences with PetSmart in the past, but they were never really a big deal to me.
However, this one was an exception.
At about 3:30pm yesterday (8/11) I phoned the 7th Ave. location to inquire if they had otocincluses. For those who are wondering, an otocinclus is an algae sucking catfish. Inexpensive, very active, and frequently popular.
Anyway, after getting past the phone tree, someone answered the phone, but it sounded like the phone was wandering around the store in someone's pocket.
Then, a female voice: "Hello?". Not even a retail greeting.
I replied, "Yes, I'd like to speak with someone in fish."
I think I heard her say, "Hold on." Then I was put back in her pocket to wander around the store some more. For a few minutes.
I hung up, and called again. Got past the phone tree...and I was still in her pocket.
One more time....same thing.
Finally, I hung up again, called again.
A male answered the phone: "Hello. Thank you for calling PetSmart. How can I help you?"
I replied, "I'd like to speak with someone in fish please."
"Someone in fish?"
"Yes"
He put me on hold...for several minutes. I hung up and called again. Same guy answered.
"I'd like to speak with someone in fish please."
"What'd you need?"
"I just have one question."
Then I heard him cover the phone and ask another male, "Did you wanna take a question about fish?"
Another male picks up.
"Hi. How can I help you?"
"I just wanted to see if you have any otocincluses today."
"I'm not even sure what that is."
My immediate response, "You gotta be kidding me."
He asked, "Could you spell it?"
"O-t-o-c-i-n-c-l-u-s"
I heard typing...twice. Then he put me on hold. Then, a female who seemed to have the air of a supervisor/manager picked up.
"Hi. What was your question?"
"I just wanted to see if you have any otocincluses today."
"Let me check."
After a brief hold she returned, "Yes we do."
That entire interaction took all of 30 minutes...for one simple question. Nothing was settled until a supervisor arrived. It shouldn't have come to that, and the call shouldn't have been handled that way.
